title: Tuples
test_conventions: Tests are Python assert snippets executed AFTER the learner's code, in the same namespace, one snippet at a time. Everything the learner's code printed is available to tests as the string variable __stdout__. expected_output comparisons are exact after stripping trailing whitespace on each line (and trailing blank lines). tests[].visible defaults to true; visible:false tests are hidden and always carry a failure_message. For fill_blank, blanks in starter_code are written ___ and are filled in order; every alternative in blanks[].answer must pass the tests. For parsons, lines are shown shuffled; correct_order lists, for each position of the solution, the index into lines; distractors are extra lines that must not be used. For predict, expected_output must be one of choices; for debug with expected_output the fixed program's stdout must match it exactly. The learner source code is available to tests as the string __source__.

notes: A tuple uses round brackets and is indexed and sliced like a list.
A tuple cannot be changed after it is created.
notes_tr: Tuple yuvarlak parantez kullanır; liste gibi indekslenir ve dilimlenir.

exercises.explanation: point[1] is the second item, 7; the tuple has 2 items. + joins two tuples into a new tuple (3, 7, 9).

misconceptions.3 2\n(3, 7, 9): Indexes start at 0, so point[1] is the SECOND item, 7.
misconceptions.7 2\n(3, 7) (9,): The + operator joins the tuples into one new tuple.
misconceptions.7 3\n(3, 7, 9): len(point) is evaluated before any new tuple is built: point still has two items.

misconceptions_tr.7 3\n(3, 7, 9): len(point) yeni tuple kurulmadan önce hesaplanır: point'te hâlâ iki eleman var.

notes: To 'change' a tuple, convert to a list, edit, convert back.
The result is a NEW tuple; the old one is not modified.
notes_tr: Bir tuple'ı 'değiştirmek' için listeye çevir, düzenle, tekrar tuple yap.
Sonuç YENİ bir tuple'dır; eskisi değişmez.

exercises.code:

exercises.explanation: list(t) builds a separate list. Appending to that list never touches the tuple t.

misconceptions.(1, 2, 3, 4) [1, 2, 3, 4]: Tuples cannot be changed. list(t) made a separate list; t stays (1, 2, 3).
misconceptions.(1, 2, 3) [1, 2, 3]: l.append(4) did run, so l has four items.
misconceptions.[1, 2, 3, 4] (1, 2, 3): The print order is t first, then l.

exercises.explanation_tr: list(t) ayrı bir liste oluşturur. Bu listeye ekleme yapmak t tuple'ına hiç dokunmaz.

misconceptions_tr.(1, 2, 3, 4) [1, 2, 3, 4]: Tuple'lar değiştirilemez. list(t) ayrı bir liste yaptı; t (1, 2, 3) olarak kalır.
misconceptions_tr.(1, 2, 3) [1, 2, 3]: l.append(4) çalıştı, bu yüzden l'de dört eleman var.
misconceptions_tr.[1, 2, 3, 4] (1, 2, 3): Yazdırma sırası önce t, sonra l'dir.

exercises.prompt: In your own words: what is the difference between a list and a tuple, and when would you choose a tuple?
exercises.prompt_tr: Kendi cümlelerinle: liste ile tuple arasındaki fark nedir ve ne zaman tuple seçerdin?
exercises.model_answer: A list can be changed after it is created, a tuple cannot (it is immutable). A tuple is a good choice for data that should stay fixed, such as coordinates or the days of the week.
exercises.model_answer_tr: Liste oluşturulduktan sonra değiştirilebilir, tuple ise değiştirilemez (immutable). Hafta günleri ya da koordinatlar gibi sabit kalması gereken veriler için tuple iyi bir seçimdir.
